label: Nitrogen dioxide in the lower atmosphere (OMI)
verdict: Nitrogen dioxide in the lower atmosphere (OMI) (all months, 2005-2025): the trend is -1.8 10^15 molecules/cm2 per decade, about -3.5 10^15 molecules/cm2 over the whole period. It is NOT statistically significant: p = 0.45 >= 0.05. That does not prove there is no trend; the change is not distinguishable from year-to-year variability with this many years. A longer record or a larger region can make a real trend significant. Neighbouring years are correlated (carry-over r = 0.90), so the test counts about 3 independent years instead of 21; ignoring that would overstate significance.

dataset.label: Nitrogen dioxide in the lower atmosphere (OMI)
dataset.source: OMI/Aura NO2 tropospheric column, cloud-screened, daily L3 0.25 deg v4 (monthly means computed here)
dataset.note: A gas from traffic, power plants and industry. NASA publishes it daily; the app averages each month (about 30 small requests per month, so a long period takes several minutes the first time). Part of the instrument's view has been blocked since 2007 (row anomaly): fewer measurements per day
